reviews.comment: This professor is just straight up a bully. I struggled in his class throughout the semester, and when I reached out to him to potentially improve he basically told me I wasn't smart enough and I wasn't trying hard enough in his class, even though I studied the most for his class. He made the tests hard;seems like only to feed his ego. Impossible!!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I have had. He is obviously very passionate about the material and that makes the lectures very engaging and fun. The exams were difficult but he never tried to make the class harder than it needed to be.

Dr. MacKenzie is an amazing person and enjoys teaching, but his exams were difficult. His exams are based on the lecture and really puts your understanding of the information to the test. It is a tough class, but if you're willing to put the work you will do fine. I really struggled throughout the semester, but also had another tough class as well
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. MacKenzie was the best professor that I have had at Texas A&M University, he is a great lecturer and just an amazing teacher overall. If you are planning on taking this course in Honors, his class is a no-brainer.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a hard class - but mackenzie makes it bearable. You can tell he is super passionate about the material which makes it more interesting. He is always willing to help students, but makes sure you are really working to get the grade. Tests are difficult - FR heavy and he wants you to answer it a certain way. I would take for another bio course
Dr. Mackenzie was an amazing lecturer, but his tests are mainly free response, so you really have to study.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DMac was a BIG struggle. He really loves teaching this course & is super interested in the topics so lectures for every single minute of the class. You will only do good in class if you learn and memorize every example he mentioned in class. I went to every class, but had to record the lectures to catch every example. GO TO CLASS & TAKE GOOD NOTES!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: MacKenzie's test were ridiculously hard; even reading the textbooks and attending his lectures were barely enough to get me C's on the tests. He was a very kind professor but made sure that you struggled to get the grade you wanted.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr MacKenzie had unrealistic expectations of his students on tests and in the very first lecture said that no one would ever get a 100 on a test. do not choose brian as your ta because he is the most discouraging person I have ever met. he is ruthless when grading and even once wrote on a paper that it was wholly inadequate.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. MacKenzie is an incredibly expectant professor. I enjoyed this class and his passion but he was tough on the tests and often had unrealistic expectations on the information that you needed to know. I know many of us are crossing our fingers that there is a curve at the end. Do well in the lab and you will give yourself a lot more leeway.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Duncan is great. His tests are really difficult. The material is A LOT. But the class grade isn't solely based on exams, which is awesome... If you're a poor test taker, you can still get at least a B if you do well on other assignments. Ask your question out loud because the class is based on points and that gives you an extra. Don't procrastinate
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. MacKenzie has a clear passion for biology. He teaches with an excitement and joy unmatched by any other prof. Class is certainly a challenge. Make sure to study everything on his slide in good detail because he will ask about it. Great Prof!

Dr. MacKenzie was definitely a really nice guy and knew a lot about the subject. I found his tests very hard and I always came out of them not feeling confident. Since it was an honors course, it was curved a ton (I had an 84 which ended up being an A), so don't worry too much about the end grade. Also I recommend going to review sessions.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: A beyond brilliant professor that presents endocrinology in a way that is both intellectually stimulating yet achievable. You have to come to class and pay attention, but it is beyond worth it. It is because of Dr. MacKenzie that I chose to go into this field, and the knowledge he gave landed me in one of the best endocrinology labs in the country.

The class was close to impossible. The tests are graded with the expectation that you memorized every single thing he said in class or you wouldn't get full credit on short answer. Was never clear about the curve and kept making tests harder even though we were struggling. Hardest class I've ever taken. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: tough but rewarding class. One of the best biology courses i've taken here. i think i can speak for everyone when i say that he cares about his students and the material. plus his son is really cute. A+
Hand down the best professor I have ever had. Knows his material and is very helpful. Exams are difficult but going to the lecture helps.
Hands down the best professor I have ever had. Knows his material and very helpful to students. Exams are difficult but going to the lecture helps.
A professor that has a lifetime influence on his students - responsible for more successful physicians and scientists than any other faculty member on campus.
